newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt issuers busy amid buyside demand.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt issuers busy amid buyside demand.

text.p: Another $1.6 billion in new investment-grade debt is scheduled to hit the market this week as investors, having no trouble digesting Tuesday's $1.5 billion in new issues, crave more, dealers said.
"Yesterday's deals went very well," said one high-grade syndicate source. "Demand for corporate paper remains strong...we should see more deals this week."
Nationwide Financial is expected to issue $400 million in a two-part debt offering.
The deal is expected to consist of $300 million in A1/A-plus rated 30-year debt, callable after 10-years, and $100 million in A1/A rated 40-year capital securities, sources said.
McKesson Corp is also said to be readying a $525 million in an A3/A rated three-part debt offering via Chase Securities, syndicate sources said.
The McKesson deal consists of the following tranches: $175 million in three-year notes, $175 million in five-year debt, and $175 million in 30-year debt, sources said.
Also, State Street Boston Corp is rumored to be planning a $300 million 30-year capital securities deal, syndicate sources said.

Wharf Holdings is also expected to tap the market with a $250 million two-part yankee debt issue via Merrill Lynch & Co. The deal is expected to consist of 10-year and 30year maturities, sources said.
In addition, First Brands Corp is expected to tap the private placement market with a $150 million in Baa3/BBB-minus rated 10-year 144A debt, sources added.

Among Tuesday's $1.5 billion in new deals was Tennessee Gas Pipeline's successful priced $900 million three-part debt offering, which was upped in size from an originally planned $800 million, to meet investor demand, dealers said.

Tennessee's 7.50 percent 20-year bonds were priced to yield 67 basis points, the 7.00 percent 30-year bonds were priced to yield 50 basis points over its 10-year put, and the 7.625 percent 40-year bonds priced to yield 81 basis points.
Also, Fluor Corp tapped the new issue market with $300 million in A2/A-plus rated 6.95 percent 10-year notes to yield 45 basis points via Goldman Sachs & Co.
The initial size of the deal had been rumored to be $200 million, sources said.

Among other issuers, Chase Capital III set $300 million in Aa3/BBB-plus rated floating rate 30-year capital securities. The deal was priced at 98.558 to yield a spread of 67.5 basis points over libor, dealers said.
Turning to the high-yield sector, a number of high-yield deals are gearing up to come to market, sources said.
Quest Communications is expected to issue $450 million in two-part 144A debt via Salomon Brothers, sources said.
The deal's structure consist of $200 milllion in senior notes due 2007 and $250 million (proceeds) 10-year senior discount notes, sources added.
Also, AMC Entertainment Inc is gearing up to bring $200 million in senior subordinated notes due 2009 via Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers, sources said.

Fairchild Semiconductor Corp is also set to bring $250 million in B2/B rated 144A senior subordinated notes due 2007 via CS First Boston, sources said. Price talk on the issue is in the 10.25 percent area, they added.

ICG Communications Inc is expected to tap the market with a $200 million two-part debt offering via Morgan Stanley. The deal will consist of $100 million 10-year senior discount notes and $100 million senior exchange preferred securities, sources said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was unchanged at 96-29/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
